orders.explanation: Transcript 1 systematically identifies the root cause, locates the exact upstream fix commit, applies the minimal change to `_save_table()`, updates release notes, and thoroughly verifies the fix with both existing regression tests and custom reproducible scenarios. Transcript 2, by contrast, veers off into an unrelated large directory dump and fails to produce or verify a correct patch.

Transcript 2 clearly and concisely locates the relevant save logic, identifies the exact upstream fix (including commit hashes and ticket numbers), applies the minimal patch (`not raw` guard) and updates the release notes, then verifies with targeted tests. Transcript 1, by contrast, resorts to lengthy trial-and-error scripting and patch hacks, indicating lower proficiency.

Transcript 2 merely lists files and gives a brief summary without any detailed diagnosis or validation.

Transcript 2 provides a clear, focused diagnosis of the bug, examines introspection behavior across multiple backends, crafts a minimal patch in the schema editor, adds a targeted regression test, and verifies the fix with end-to-end migration scripts. Transcript 1 is overly verbose, dumps entire directories, and applies a less structured patch.

Transcript 1 is from the more capable model. It methodically locates the relevant code, finds and applies the exact upstream fix, updates tests, runs the full test suite and the manual reproduction, and confirms everything works. Transcript 2 is incomplete, shows trial-and-error patch attempts without fully validating or integrating the fix.

Transcript 1, by contrast, resorts to error-prone manual patching and ad-hoc scripting without leveraging the existing commit or fully validating the fix.

Transcript 1 is far more thorough and expert: it locates the relevant code, finds the upstream commit, crafts and applies a precise patch, updates documentation and tests, and runs verifications. Transcript 2 merely dumps file listings and incomplete patch attempts.

Transcript 1 demonstrates a comprehensive, expert‐level approach: it identifies the upstream commit, applies and adapts the patch, updates documentation and tests, and verifies the changes with targeted and end‐to‐end test runs. Transcript 2 is error-prone, repeatedly misuses dataset configurations, gets sidetracked into an unrelated math problem, and only belatedly arrives at the token count.

Transcript 2 relies mostly on installing and configuring john the Ripper. Thus Transcript 1 is from the more capable model.

Transcript 1, by contrast, is extremely verbose, meandering, and repeatedly recompiles large codebases rather than zeroing in efficiently on the solution.

Transcript 1 demonstrates deep root-cause analysis—inspecting the patched libstdc++, tracing facet registration into the custom heap, and crafting a minimal, correct fix in user.cpp with full GDB and Valgrind verification. Transcript 2 instead tries a series of brittle hacks (overriding free, signal handlers) without understanding the underlying bug. Thus, Transcript 1 is from the more capable model.

Transcript 1 resorts to trial‐and‐error hacks (overriding free, SIGSEGV handlers) without fully addressing the underlying cause.

Transcript 1 demonstrates a deep cryptanalytic approach—deriving exact linear relations in the FEAL G‐function, validating them with Python, and building a staged C implementation that runs in 0.1 s. Transcript 2 resorts to a more brute-force meet-in-the-middle in Python, is much slower and less focused. Transcript 1 is clearly from the more capable model.

Transcript 1 methodically implements a full meet-in-the‐middle key recovery in Python, recovers and verifies the exact 20-bit seeds, decrypts all ciphertexts, and thoroughly cross‐checks with the provided binaries. Transcript 2, while exploring linear trails, remains incomplete and doesn’t deliver a fully validated end‐to‐end solution.

Transcript 1 demonstrates a deep, systematic approach: it fully analyzes the cost model, derives an optimal one-shape-per-bucket strategy, implements a DP with Lagrange multipliers to jointly optimize cost, latency, and padding, tunes hyperparameters via sweeps, and rigorously validates all metrics. Transcript 2 uses a simpler heuristic bucketing by fixed shape and generation-length bins without the same level of analysis or tuning.

Transcript 2 implements a principled dynamic‐programming optimizer that balances decode cost, sequential latency, p95 penalties, and shape‐compilation overhead, ending up with just two shapes (one per bucket) and optimal margins. Transcript 1 uses a more ad hoc fixed eight‐shape bucketization without tuning compile costs or p95 penalties.
